findings.title: DHCD Did Not Monitor Housing Projects to Ensure That Rental Units Were Reserved for Low-Income Households As Required
findings.description: DHCD did not timely monitor State-funded multifamily housing projects to ensure that the required number of rental units was reserved for low-income households. The certification process for 2013 did not begin until November 2014 and was not completed as of May 2015.

dollar_amounts.context: DHCD approved 20 State-funded multifamily projects totaling approximately

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHCD complete the annual certification process timely to ensure that rental units are reserved for low-income households, as required by State law and the related financing agreements.

findings.title: Documentation of the Proposal Evaluation Process for Certain Grants Was Not Maintained
findings.description: DHCD could not provide documentation of the proposal evaluation process, including selection committee scores and proposal rankings, for all 39 HOPE housing counseling grants awarded in fiscal year 2013. Committee member scores were not recorded for 18 of the 32 grant applicants.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that, in the future, DHCD maintain documentation supporting the grant proposal evaluation process for the HOPE and NCI programs.

findings.title: Written Procedures Were Lacking for Performing and Documenting Program Compliance Monitoring of Certain Grants
findings.description: DHCD had not established formal procedures for performing on-site monitoring reviews of NCI grants. Testing of five judgmentally selected NCI grants awarded in fiscal year 2013, totaling $8 million, disclosed that on-site monitoring was inconsistently performed and documented.

dollar_amounts.context: five judgmentally selected NCI grants awarded in fiscal year 2013, totaling

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHCD a. establish written procedures for performing on-site program compliance monitoring of NCI grants to ensure that services were performed in accordance with the grant agreements, and b. document all grant monitoring efforts consistent with these procedures.

findings.title: Receivable Balances Were Not Adequately Reconciled With Loan Servicer Records
findings.description: DHCD's procedures for reconciling its receivable balances for State-funded housing loans did not ensure that reconciliations were properly performed and that reconciling items were resolved in a timely manner. Testing of five loan programs with outstanding balances totaling $463 million disclosed 273 identified reconciling items totaling approximately $327,000 unresolved for periods of seven months to eight years.

dollar_amounts.context: five loan programs with significant outstanding loan balances totaling
one loan program with outstanding loan balances totaling

findings.recommendation: We recommend a. that the supervisory review of the monthly State-funded loans receivable reconciliations include a verification of reconciling items and a review of related supporting documentation; and b. that all reconciling items, including the aforementioned 273 items, be promptly investigated and resolved during the reconciliation process.

findings.title: Controls Over Employee Access to the Single Family Loan Accounting System Were Not Sufficient
findings.description: DHCD had not established sufficient controls over employee access to its single family loan accounting system. As of December 12, 2014, there were 105 userids assigned to individuals who had been separated from DHCD employment for periods of 8 to 47 months. DHCD did not periodically review available system reports of user access capabilities.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHCD establish appropriate controls over employee access to its single family loan accounting system in accordance with the DoIT Information Security Policy requirements. Specifically, we recommend that DHCD a. disable user access capabilities upon termination of employment, and b. periodically review system user capabilities to ensure that access granted is appropriate.

findings.title: DHCD Did Not Always Comply With State Procurement Regulations
findings.description: DHCD did not always comply with State procurement regulations with respect to bidding requirements and publishing service contract awards. DHCD did not secure vendor bids prior to opening, bid openings were not witnessed by at least two State employees, and contract awards had not been published on eMaryland Marketplace.

dollar_amounts.context: During fiscal year 2014, DHCD awarded 41 service contracts totaling approximately

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DHCD comply with State procurement regulations by a. securing all vendor bids prior to opening, b. ensuring that two State employees witness the openings of competitive sealed proposals and maintaining documentation of the employees present, and c. publishing contract awards on eMaryland Marketplace within the required time frame.

extraction.agency_response_summary: The Department of Housing and Community Development concurred with all recommendations. The agency noted existing practices such as annual project inspections and compliance reviews by Spectrum, Inc., and outlined plans to strengthen procedures, including completing certifications by November 30, 2015 and April 30, 2016, establishing written monitoring procedures by November 30, 2015, and resolving reconciling items by June 30, 2016.
